If you imported a certificate into ACM, you\\nmust monitor the expiration date of the certificate and renew it before it expires. Use the UpdateDataSource operation or the AWS Management Console.\\n5. Start a sync and confirm it completes successfully with the new certificate.\\n6. After the sync succeeds, remove the old certificate from the Entra app registration and delete the old `.p12` object from Amazon S3\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-sharepoint-troubleshooting.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Checking AWS docs for RHUI certificate expiration fix on copied RHEL AMIs"}

{"id": "4ba95b59-9029-4936-9694-79f760299d55", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "That confirms the root cause and gives me the official package names. Here's the full picture and fix.

## Why this is happening

RHUI client certs embedded in AWS's RHEL PAYG AMIs are **region-specific** — the RHUI package that ships in the us-east-1 AMI contains a cert/config pointing at us-east-1's RHUI content delivery servers, with a validity window tied to that AMI's build. When you copy the AMI to us-west-2 and launch there, the instance is still carrying the us-east-1 RHUI client package. Two things commonly go wrong at once:

1. The cert is scoped/signed for the source region's RHUI endpoints, not the destination region's.
2. Over time, that embedded cert simply expires (your `enddate` in the past confirms this) — AWS periodically rotates/reissues RHUI client certs, and a copied AMI frozen at build time will eventually carry a stale one.

Either way, the result is the same: `SSL peer certificate was not OK` talking to `rhui-X.<region>.aws.ce.redhat.com` and metadata download failures for `rhel-9-appstream-rhui-rpms` / `rhel-9-baseos-rhui-rpms`.

**AWS's position:** don't copy RHEL PAYG AMIs cross-region and expect RHUI to keep working — launch PAYG RHEL instances from AWS's own published RHEL AMI in the target region instead. But if you're stuck with the existing instance, you can repair RHUI in place.

## Fix: reinstall the region-correct RHUI client config

This has to be done on the instance itself (SSM Session Manager or SSH):

```bash
# 1. Back up current RHUI state
sudo mkdir -p ~/rhui-backup
sudo cp -ra /etc/yum.repos.d /etc/pki/rhui ~/rhui-backup/

# 2. Find and remove the stale RHUI packages
sudo rpm -qa | grep rhui
sudo yum remove -y $(rpm -qa | grep rhui)

# 3. Reinstall the RHUI client config package for RHEL 9 x86_64,
#    pulling it fresh so it's correct for us-west-2.
#    AWS publishes this as an RPM you install directly from the AWS-hosted URL —
#    get the current URL/version for RHEL 9 from AWS's RHUI documentation,
#    since the package version changes over time, e.g.:
sudo yum install -y https://rhui3.<region>.aws.ce.redhat.com/pulp/repos/.../rhui-client-config-server-9-<version>.noarch.rpm

# 4. Clean yum cache and test
sudo yum clean all
sudo yum repolist
sudo yum update --disablerepo="*" --enablerepo="rhel-9-appstream-rhui-rpms,rhel-9-baseos-rhui-rpms"
```

The exact RPM filename/version for the "rhui-client-config-server-9" package changes as AWS rotates certs, so I don't want to hand you a URL that might already be stale — I'd rather confirm the current one than guess.

**The more reliable alternative:** spin up a throwaway RHEL 9 PAYG instance from AWS's native us-west-2 AMI (not a copy), grab its working `/etc/pki/rhui/*` and `rhui-client-config-server-9` RPM, and copy those onto your affected instance. That guarantees a cert that's valid for us-west-2 right now.

Want me to look up the current RHUI client config package URL/version for RHEL 9 in us-west-2, or help you script pulling the cert from a fresh native AMI instance?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
